F.1.notes: The metric counts offline fitted models. The test also records fitted_models_used_by_default_worlds (0) and fitted_models_with_verified_opt_in_use (1): no default world consumes a fitted model yet; that is wave 2 (D-15). repeat_consumption (creator_return@1) is weak (held-out AUC 0.51).

F.2.status_claim: implemented and measured locally: content_consumption@1 (KuaiRand random exposure) and commercial_response@1 (Criteo randomised trials) qualify and beat their baselines on held-out data
F.2.notes: The E3 review (prespecified compute budget 100 us/row) keeps commercial_response's constant-effect baseline because the T-learner costs 121 us/row through the registry predictor; the runtime therefore serves the randomised ITT effect without heterogeneity. The 64-type table a world would use is cheap, but the plan timed the registry predictor; flagged for the reviewer.

SP-5.4.status_claim: implemented and passing locally: the parser reads every register table (the blank-line bug that dropped 17 rows is fixed and tested), a record covers exactly the mechanism whose id it carries (module rows no longer vouch for decisions; population decisions, consumption-engine parameter groups and runtime decision models are important mechanisms of their own), every false 'fitted in-world' row was corrected, and every claimed in-world use is verified (5 opt-in claims verified, 0 default claims)
SP-5.4.notes: Zero missing records is reached by honest records: most population, social and commerce mechanisms are 'plausible, unvalidated'. An in-world mechanism cannot be labelled empirically fitted while its in-world use is 'none'. The static verification of an opt-in claim checks that the module's package references the model or its runtime decision; a 'default' claim additionally needs an in-world probe (none exist yet).

SP-5.5.status_claim: implemented and passing locally: E3 and E4 plans committed before any review or fit (commit order checked from git); the E4 selection rule (compute budget, long-horizon drift, test confirmation) is recomputed from the cards; every E3 review's kept contender is recomputed from its numbers
SP-5.5.notes: Under the prespecified E3 rule three reviews keep a non-checkpoint contender (session_rate -> C2 rule; news_click -> popularity baseline; commercial_response -> constant-effect baseline) and the runtime serves them. The E2 amendment written after run-1 test metrics is now flagged (amendments_after_test_exposure) for the reviewer, as the audit asked.

limitations: No default world uses any fitted model; the runtime API is ready for the unified population (wave 2, D-15). The only in-world use is an opt-in feed configuration whose contract (MiniLM affinity space) current worlds cannot honestly satisfy.
MIND licence acceptance is a user decision (BLOCKERS B-1); news_click@1 and news_click_semantic@1 remain non-commercial research artifacts.
All E4 models are observational; the price coefficient of product_demand is an association, star_cascade's self-excitation mixes contagion with referrals and trending feedback.
creator_return@1 (repeat consumption) barely discriminates (AUC 0.51): repeat consumption of a creator is rare in KuaiRand-Pure.

The E3 drift criterion (any significant difference) is strict: it rejects news_click@1's checkpoint for a 0.0003 calibration drift difference and session_rate's gamma-Poisson for its known upward drift; a future plan should add a practical-significance margin. Not changed after seeing results.
The E3 compute criterion timed the registry predictor, not the in-world path (commercial_response's type table).

Plan deviations recorded in the reviews/reports: watch_duration rule quantiles computed exactly by bisection instead of 2,000-draw Monte Carlo; session_rate's forward simulation uses the card's test window (05-05..05-08) rather than 05-01..05-08; customer_return's long-horizon check reports monthly stability but not the 30/60-day cohort retention curves; product_demand's forward simulation keeps the observed 4-week buyer counts.
star_cascade's prespecified GBDT Poisson candidate diverged numerically (deviance 8.5e4) and lost; it was not refitted after test exposure.
GH Archive event tables keep exact timestamps, so linkage to the public archive remains possible for someone who downloads it; the tables stay local and only aggregate parameters are committed.
